rv.q: Its lovely score, engaging performers and heartfelt story soon reassert themselves.
Those elements aside, this is an unusually solacing musical about the isolation of illness, the comfort of other people and the refuge of art.
It's when the Lazours entangle the audience in the action that Night Side Songs achieves liftoff.
Night Side Songs, occasional lyrical hiccups aside, assembles a pensive and at times sparkling experience of community in the face of darkness.
Night Side Songs can assuredly boast of a stalwart cast, directed by deft Lazours collaborator Taibi Magar.
But I couldn’t help thinking that the kaleidoscopic quality of “Night Side Songs” dilutes its impact, and – to extend Sontag’s metaphor — turns us into tourists.
Night Side Songs is beautiful, aching, passionate, and heartfelt—and utterly surprising in the gentle way it guides the audience into thinking about our own lives and wanting to be better.
The effect is often lovely, matching the tone of a show that centers the collective nature of illness and care-giving.
But for all its earnestness and yearning for connectivity, this song cycle about life, illness, and death flatlines.

cn.t: This gentle chamber musical about illness and mortality earns praise for its intimate, participatory approach and folk score, though some critics find it too earnest and emotionally flat despite strong performances.

vr.q: Night Side Songs is generally an unusual piece of theater that you should go see for that reason... I find the characters all interesting and sympathetic, but I really wanted to get more into their lives and know more about them.
In some ways, there was too much scenework for there to be a music-driven emotional arc, and conversely there was too much audience involvement for the storytelling to take hold.
